'''David Firth''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FBA}} (born 22 December 1957) is a British [[statistician]].<ref name=whoswho/>  He is [[Emeritus Professor]] in the Department of Statistics at the [[University of Warwick]].<ref name=whoswho/>

==Education==
Firth was born and went to school in [[Wakefield]].<ref name=whoswho/> He studied mathematics at the [[University of Cambridge]]<ref name=whoswho/> and completed his PhD in statistics at [[Imperial College London]],<ref name=whoswho/> supervised by [[David Cox (statistician)|Sir David Cox]].<ref name=mathgene/>

==Research==

Firth is known for his development of a general method<ref name=Bka1993/> for reducing the [[Bias of an estimator|bias]] of [[maximum likelihood estimation]] in parametric [[statistical models]].  The method has seen application in a wide variety of research fields, especially with [[logistic regression]] analysis where the reduced-bias estimates also have reduced [[variance]] and are always finite;<ref name=Bka2021/> the latter property overcomes the frequently encountered problem of [[Separation (statistics)|separation]], which causes maximum likelihood estimates to be infinite.  The original paper published in 1993<ref name=Bka1993/> has been cited more than 4000 times according to [https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?user=rtOYz5YAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao Google Scholar].

Together with a PhD student, Renée de Menezes, Firth also established the generality of the method of [[Quasi-variance|quasi variances]], a device for summarizing economically the estimated effects of a categorical predictor variable in a statistical model.<ref name=SocMeth2003/><ref name=Bka2004/>

==Applied work==

Firth developed (in collaboration with [[John Curtice]]) a new statistical approach to the design and analysis of election-day exit polls for [[United Kingdom general elections overview|UK General Elections]].  The new methods have been used at UK General Elections since 2005 to produce the widely broadcast close-of-polls forecast of seats in the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]].<ref name=JRSS2008/>

==Awards and honours==
Firth was elected as a [[Fellow of the British Academy]] in 2008. He was the recipient of the [[Royal Statistical Society]]'s [[Guy Medal]] in Bronze in 1998 and in Silver in 2012.  With Dr Heather Turner he won the [[John Chambers (statistician)#John M. Chambers Statistical Software Award|John M Chambers Statistical Software Award]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 2007, for the [https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/gnm ''gnm'' package] which facilitates working with generalized nonlinear models (a synthesis of [[nonlinear regression]] and [[generalized linear models]]) in [[R (programming language)|R]].

He is a former Editor of the [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society#Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (Statistical Methodology)|Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (Statistical Methodology)]].
